description: Dashboard style gallery: complete, themeable reference dashboards an agent can pick from by style family, use case or mode. Each entry lives in site/dashboards/<id>/ (index.html + style.css + app.js + thumb.jpg). Edit here, then run node scripts/build.mjs and node scripts/dashboards-check.mjs.

style_families.name: Cinematic & atmospheric
style_families.blurb: Dark, moody, scenic backdrops (painted or photographic) with glass panels and one warm accent. For consumer products that should feel like an experience.

style_families.name: Glass & glow
style_families.blurb: Frosted translucent panels over gradients or blurred color fields, soft glows. Modern, techy, premium.

style_families.name: Minimal & airy
style_families.blurb: Lots of white space, hairlines, one accent, quiet type. Calm tools people use all day.

style_families.name: Bento grid
style_families.blurb: Tiles of different sizes in a tight grid, each tile one idea. Great for overviews and product showcases.

style_families.name: Data-dense pro
style_families.blurb: Compact tables, many small charts, tight spacing, monospace numbers. Trading, ops, analytics power users.

style_families.name: Soft & friendly
style_families.blurb: Rounded shapes, pastel fills, playful illustration-free warmth. Health, education, personal apps.

style_families.name: Editorial
style_families.blurb: Big serif headlines, magazine layout, image-led storytelling. Brands, content, luxury.

style_families.name: Bold & graphic
style_families.blurb: High contrast, saturated blocks, heavy type, brutalist or neo-brutalist edges. Creative tools, youth brands.

style_families.name: Dark neon
style_families.blurb: Near-black canvas with vivid neon accents and gradients. Gaming, crypto, music, nightlife.

style_families.name: Tactile & neumorphic
style_families.blurb: Soft extruded surfaces, depth, physical-feeling controls. Smart home, devices, audio.

dashboards.name: Horizon Weather
dashboards.summary: A cinematic weather home: painted sunset landscape behind glass panels, an editorial serif headline, a 7-day forecast strip with a glowing selected day, a smooth gold temperature curve and a mood card.
best_for: Consumer apps where the feeling matters as much as the numbers
Travel, outdoor, hospitality or lifestyle dashboards
Landing-page heroes for a data product
avoid_when: Dense business data (tables, many KPIs): the scenery competes with numbers
Light-mode-only brands
Low-end devices that struggle with backdrop blur

layout.structure: Fixed left sidebar (brand, 5-item nav, quote) · top bar (pill search, bell, avatar) · hero (headline left, current conditions right) over a painted scene · 7-day strip · 3 columns: area chart, details list, story card · popular-locations row
layout.responsive: ≤1180px: chart spans full width above details + story · ≤960px: sidebar becomes a top bar, hero stacks · ≤640px: single column, icon-only nav, day strip scrolls horizontally

components: Area chart with range toggle and hover/focus values
Image story card with serif quote
dashboards.signature: Code-drawn sunset landscape (SVG, themed by CSS variables) fading into the dark UI, with a gold glow ring on the selected day.

source.note: Recreated in original code from a user-supplied concept screenshot. Brand name, photos and copy were replaced; the landscape is drawn in SVG. The source image is not stored in the repo.

dashboards.name: Pulsar Analytics
dashboards.summary: A dark neon product-analytics overview: glossy metric orbs that switch the main chart, layered violet and mint wave areas over a purple floor glow, a ticked uptime dial and gradient pillar bars.
best_for: Product, web or infrastructure analytics for a technical audience
Wall displays and status pages that are read at a glance
Brands that already live in dark mode
avoid_when: Long tables or text-heavy admin screens: the glow tires the eye
Conservative or regulated brands (banking, legal, healthcare)
Print or export-first reporting

layout.structure: Top bar (brand, 4-item nav, pill search, range toggle, bell, avatar) · 3 columns at 1440px: 288px left rail (uptime dial, health donut, hourly bars) · fluid centre (4 metric orbs, wave chart, 3 sparkline tiles) · 304px right rail (channel pillars, top events, regions) · 18px gaps
layout.responsive: ≤1180px: centre column spans full width on top, rails sit side by side below, search hides · ≤960px: nav wraps under the bar, orbs 2×2 · ≤640px: single column, orbs stack, chart 200px tall

components: Metric orbs (toggle buttons that switch the chart)
Two-series wave area chart with hover/focus values
dashboards.signature: Violet and mint wave areas rising out of a blurred purple floor glow, with glossy sphere-like metric buttons above.

source.note: Recreated in original code from a user-supplied concept render of a dark analytics board. The render had no readable text, so brand, labels, metrics and all data are invented. Charts, dial and orbs are drawn in SVG and CSS. The source image is not stored in the repo.

dashboards.name: Solstice Energy
dashboards.summary: A cinematic solar-monitoring board: a thick gradient sun-path arc rises over a code-drawn mountain range, with generation and load curves on a teal grid, a readout strip, storage dials and round site thumbnails.
best_for: Energy, solar, climate or outdoor-equipment monitoring
A single hero metric that follows the time of day
Control-room or kiosk screens with a strong visual identity
avoid_when: Many records to scan or edit: the hero scene takes most of the first screen
Brands that need a neutral, corporate look
Data with no natural day cycle or location

layout.structure: Slim top bar (brand, 4-item nav, date, 2 icon buttons) · 12-column grid at 1440px, 18px gaps: 3-column rail (today's total, strings table, self-powered ring) + 9-column hero (sun arc scene, hourly chart, 6-item readout strip) · then 2×2 half-width panels (output bars with range toggle, 4 storage dials, hourly load bars, 4 site thumbnails)
layout.responsive: ≤1180px: hero full width on top, rail becomes a two-column panel below · ≤760px: single column, hero chart 130px, readout strip 3×2, dials and sites 2×2

components: Sun-path arc scene with movable sun
Two-series hourly line chart (pick an hour)
dashboards.signature: A thick yellow-to-orange-to-pink arc tracing the sun's path, cut by faceted orange mountains drawn in SVG; the sun dot moves to the hour you pick.

source.note: Recreated in original code from a user-supplied concept render with no readable text. The domain (solar monitoring), brand, labels and all data are invented. The mountain photo-style art and the round thumbnails were replaced with SVG and CSS landscapes themed by variables. The source image is not stored in the repo.

dashboards.name: Kumo Payroll
dashboards.summary: A moonlit payroll overview: a code-drawn ink landscape with a gold moon, layered hills and a blossom branch sits behind one dark, gold-edged panel holding KPI tiles, a gross/net bar chart, a deductions donut and time-off ring.
best_for: HR, payroll or people tools that want a calm, premium feeling
Hospitality, wellness or boutique brands with an illustrated identity
Monthly summaries with a handful of headline figures
avoid_when: Dense employee tables or bulk editing: the single framed panel limits width
Brands that need a neutral enterprise look
Screens that must fill a wide monitor edge to edge

layout.structure: Fixed illustrated scene behind the page · one centred panel, max 1240px, offset 210px from the top so the moon shows · inside: 216px sidebar (brand, 7-item nav, wave pattern) + 12-column main grid, 16px gaps: header with pay-period stepper · 4 KPI tiles · trend chart (7 cols) + deductions (5 cols) · time off (6) + next steps (6)
layout.responsive: ≤1080px: sidebar becomes a scrolling top nav, KPIs 2×2, cards stack · ≤640px: panel offset 130px, icon-only nav, period stepper full width, donut and legend stack

components: Sidebar nav with gold active pill
Tinted KPI tiles with change vs. last month
dashboards.signature: A glowing gold moon, ink-line hills and a cherry-blossom branch drawn in SVG behind a dark panel with a thin gold edge.

source.note: Recreated in original code from a user-supplied concept illustration of a payroll dashboard. Brand name, labels, copy and figures were rewritten. The painted moon, hills and blossoms are redrawn as SVG themed by CSS variables; the pagoda, koi and lotus artwork were left out. The source image is not stored in the repo.

dashboards.name: Canopy Reforest
dashboards.summary: An organic reforestation tracker in forest green, bark brown and tan: a leafy code-drawn hero with a big rounded headline, a deep green band of four site figures and six soft, colour-blocked tiles for species, planting, soil, tasks and crews.
best_for: Sustainability, conservation, farming or garden projects
Public-facing progress pages that mix a landing-page hero with live figures
Community or volunteer tools that should feel welcoming
avoid_when: Dense operational data or long tables
Finance, security or other serious, high-precision domains
Products that need many chart colours: the palette is deliberately narrow

layout.structure: Centred 1240px column, 20px gaps · top bar (brand, 4-item nav, bell) · 380px hero (copy left, leaf artwork right, CTA + site switcher) · 4-column metrics band · 3×2 grid of colour-blocked tiles (species bars, monthly planting bars, soil gauges, landscape tile, checklist, crews)
layout.responsive: ≤980px: tiles 2 columns, metrics band 2×2 · ≤640px: single column, leaves move above the headline, site switcher and CTA full width

components: Hero with headline, lede and pill CTA
dashboards.signature: Overlapping green and tan leaves with fine veins, drawn from one SVG path, spilling over a bark-brown wedge in the hero.

source.note: Recreated in original code from a user-supplied landing-page concept with placeholder text. It was turned into a dashboard (a reforestation tracker): brand, copy and all figures are invented. The leaf photography and the forest photo tile were replaced with SVG drawings themed by CSS variables. The source image is not stored in the repo.

dashboards.name: Ridgeline Trails
dashboards.summary: A two-tone visitor report for a trail network: a pale, quiet upper half where a misty code-drawn mountain range fades in from the right, then a wave edge into a charcoal lower half of raised pie dials, thin bars and a gold ring gauge.
best_for: Parks, outdoor, travel or architecture brands that want restraint
Weekly or seasonal reports shown on a tablet or wall display
A small number of figures that should feel like a printed page
avoid_when: Many KPIs or tables: the artwork takes the right half of the first screen
Products that need a colourful, energetic brand
Dense operational tools where every pixel carries data

layout.structure: One framed board, max 1280px, thick dark bezel · upper half (pale): centred title + period toggle, left column of 2 ring stats, 2 big numbers and a line chart, right column mountain art with a conditions card · wave-shaped edge · lower half (charcoal): 4 columns (thin bar list, 2 pie dials with legends, ring gauge + small table)
layout.responsive: ≤1080px: upper half stacks and the mountains move to a 330px strip above the wave; lower half 2×2 · ≤640px: single column, 230px mountain strip, full-width period toggle, legends as 44px rows

components: Centred wordmark header with period toggle
Thin line chart with dashed comparison
Raised pie dial with tick ring and selectable legend
dashboards.signature: Grey mountain ridges separated by bands of mist, with an ochre forest on the front slope, dissolving into the page and cut off by a wave edge into the charcoal half.

source.note: Recreated in original code from a user-supplied concept render with unreadable text. The domain (trail-network visitor report), name, labels and data are invented; the render's title wordmark was not reused. The mountain photograph was replaced with layered SVG ridges, mist gradients and triangle trees themed by CSS variables. The source image is not stored in the repo.

dashboards.name: Haven Listings
dashboards.summary: A property browser built around one large dusk scene: a code-drawn curved house glows under a blue sky, white filter tabs notch into the top edge, and a frosted card shows the selected home. Listings, price history and viewings sit below.
best_for: Real-estate, hospitality or travel products that sell one hero item at a time
Browse-and-shortlist flows with a few filters
Brands that want a showroom feeling rather than a data tool
avoid_when: Agents managing hundreds of listings: there is no table or map
Dense analytics: only one chart fits naturally
Low-end devices where backdrop blur is costly (the card falls back to a near-opaque fill)

layout.structure: 600px rounded stage with a full-bleed scene: top row (Buy pill, notched filter tab with 3 selects, Rent pill) · left 60px pill rail of 6 icons · headline and lede · white match-count card bottom-left · frosted detail card bottom-right (340px) · below: 3 cards (matching homes list, price-history line chart, viewings with a book button)
layout.responsive: ≤1100px: detail card moves under the match card, lower cards 2 columns · ≤700px: single column, filters become a stacked white card, rail turns into a horizontal pill, scene stays behind the top 470px

components: Vertical icon rail in a pill
Match count card with step-through arrow
Frosted detail card with specs and save, compare, share
Selectable listing rows with drawn thumbnails
dashboards.signature: White tabs that notch into the rounded edge of a full-bleed dusk scene, where a curved white house glows orange from inside.

source.note: Recreated in original code from a user-supplied design shot of a real-estate landing screen. The studio and product names, logo mark, headline, listing text and avatar were not reused; all homes, addresses and prices are invented. The rendered villa photo was replaced with an SVG house and sky themed by CSS variables. The source image is not stored in the repo.

dashboards.name: Aura Ring
dashboards.summary: A wellness overview for a smart ring: frosted, softly bordered cards float over a periwinkle-to-pink haze, with a two-weight headline, a score dial, thin white line charts, a code-drawn metal ring and a tappable body map.
best_for: Wearables, sleep, wellness and other consumer health products
Tablet-first overviews with a few scores and one device
Brands that want a calm, ambient feeling
avoid_when: Clinical tools where precision and density matter more than mood
Long tables or many KPIs
Interfaces that must work without colour gradients (print, e-ink)

layout.structure: Top bar (brand, centred pill tabs, bell, avatar) · 12-column grid, 18px gaps: row 1 headline (5) + score card (4) + heart-rate card (3) · rows 2–3: two small chart cards and a summary card on the left (5), device card (4) and body-map card (3) spanning both rows
layout.responsive: ≤1100px: 2 columns (headline, score + heart rate, stress + sleep, device + body, summary) and tabs scroll · ≤680px: single column, tabs on their own scrolling row

components: Centred pill tabs that switch the score
Score card with arc dial and state chip
Thin line charts with point markers
Device card with battery bar and status rows
White pill buttons with round arrow
dashboards.signature: Frosted cards with a hairline white edge over a deep periwinkle field that blooms pink on the right, and solid white pills as the only opaque elements.

source.note: Recreated in original code from a user-supplied product shot of a wellness tablet app. The product and agency names, logo, avatar photo and copy were not reused; scores and text are invented. The ring photo, 3D body figure and brain render were replaced with an SVG ring, a simple SVG figure with selectable points and a CSS orb. The source image is not stored in the repo.

dashboards.name: Lull Sleep
dashboards.summary: A one-night sleep report in soft lavender: a pastel sky hero with a crescent moon and a round score, a stage timeline you can filter by stage, a stage-split donut, a week of nights to pick from, logged habits that move the score, and bedroom conditions.
best_for: Sleep, wearables and wellness apps with a nightly report
Detail screens that explain one record with a few linked views
Consumer products where tone matters as much as numbers
avoid_when: Clinical sleep studies that need full hypnogram precision
Multi-user or admin views
Brands that need a crisp, technical feel

layout.structure: Top bar (wordmark, centred pill nav, avatar) · 250px sky hero: date, serif headline with italic second half, 3 chips, 200px round score · 12-column grid: timeline (8) + stage split (4, two rows) · night stats strip (8) · bottom row: last seven nights bar chart (5), habits (4), bedroom (3)
layout.responsive: ≤1100px: 2 columns (timeline and stats full width, split + week, habits + bedroom) · ≤700px: single column, nav on its own row, score under the headline, stats 2×2, fewer time labels

components: Sky hero with round score dial and chips
Stage timeline with stage filter chips
Bar chart that picks the night
Toggleable habit tags that change the score
dashboards.signature: A pastel blue-to-pink sky with a glowing crescent and white clouds, holding a white round score, above soft white cards with rounded lavender stage blocks.

source.note: Built in original code from a user-supplied flat shot of the same wellness screen as Aura Ring. To avoid a second copy it takes only the pastel gradient, white pills and two-weight headline, and turns them into a sleep detail page with its own layout and data. No names, logos, photos or copy from the shot were reused; sky, moon and clouds are SVG. The source image is not stored in the repo.

dashboards.name: Pearlwell Dental
dashboards.summary: A soft mint patient portal for a dental clinic: one saturated next-visit card with a code-drawn tooth and shield, a health-score ring, a booking calendar with times and dentists, a searchable treatment price list and a tappable tooth chart.
best_for: Clinics, dentists, physio and other appointment-led health services
Patient or client portals that centre on booking
Brands that want a calm, clinical-but-friendly feel
avoid_when: Clinic staff tools with schedules for many patients
Dense reporting or finance views
Brands that need a dark or dramatic look

layout.structure: 230px sticky sidebar (brand, 5 nav links, emergency note) · main: greeting header with search and avatar · 12-column grid: next visit (5) + score (3) + treatments (4, two rows) · booking card (8, two rows: month calendar left, times, dentists and confirm right) · tooth chart (4)
layout.responsive: ≤1180px: sidebar becomes a top bar, grid 2 columns · ≤700px: icon tab bar with labels, single column, calendar above times

components: Category chips and searchable price list
dashboards.signature: One deep-teal next-visit card holding a glossy white SVG tooth with a shield, set among white cards on a mint field that warms to peach in the corner.

source.note: Recreated in original code from a user-supplied concept sheet of six dental phone screens. The screens were merged into one responsive desktop portal; names, photos and copy were not reused and all patients, dentists and prices are invented. 3D tooth renders and props were replaced with an SVG tooth, shield and tooth chart. The source image is not stored in the repo.
